exercise.name: Flat Bench Cable Fly
library_steps: Place a flat bench between low pulleys and grab a handle in each hand.
Lie back with your arms open wide and elbows slightly bent.
Bring the handles together over your chest, then lower them slowly.
exercise.one_line_summary: Lying on a flat bench between two low pulleys, a handle in each hand; the softly bent arms sweep from wide open at bench level up and together over the chest. Chest does the work, the front delt helps.

setup.target: Both low, level with the chest, one each side of the bench.

movement.measure: 0 = arms out to the sides, 90 = straight up over the chest

muscles.emg: Main mover of the fly (S1); front delt only ~19 % MVIC in the fly (S2).
muscles.role: Brings the arms together; what the exercise is for.
Helps bring the arms forward; library secondary.

muscles.emg: Works as an antagonist holding the slightly bent elbow in the fly (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows bend and the hands push up.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Fly form keeps the elbows fixed.

sources.citation: Solstad TEJ, Andersen V, Shaw M, et al. 2020. A comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males. J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651.
sources.what_it_gave: Dumbbell fly vs bench press, 6RM: pectoralis major the main mover in the fly; front delt active; biceps works as an antagonist holding the slightly bent elbow.

sources.citation: Campos YAC, Vianna JM, Guimaraes MP, et al. 2020. Different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals. J Hum Kinet 75:5-14.
sources.what_it_gave: Bench press, dumbbell fly, shoulder press, lateral raise at 60 % 1RM: front delt only ~19 % MVIC in the fly; side delt highest in the lateral raise (30 %).

clip_check.check: End: hands together over the chest
Both fists closed on the handles; cables to the low pulleys
Head and back on the bench
